data.name: Campaign Guide — Current Canon
entries: {@i No Cause for Alarm: Ruins of Bellweather} is an active D&D campaign. Four level-4 PCs are about to begin Session 5. Read this current canon before preparing; played events and explicit DM corrections override abandoned plans.

entries.name: Authority and Preparation
entries: {@b PLAYED} = occurred at the table. {@b ESTABLISHED} = explicitly set by DM. {@b PREPARED} = future premise but not yet played. {@b OPEN} = uncertain and must not be invented as already true.

The former live campaign is preserved unchanged on GitHub branch archive/pre-nov-2026-canon-reset. That archive is not active canon. Only location geography/maps, selected useful rules, shops, established personal history, and actual play are carried forward.

The DM prepares deeply to understand the DNA of the world, then improvises NPC and world responses. Do not replace comprehensive preparation with a short scene script. Build maps, routines, motivations, checks, encounters, stats, consequences, and test the material.
The world exists independently of the PCs; people have jobs, disputes, relationships and priorities of their own. Not every person, site, or event relates to the central conflict.
Do not decide outcomes or destinies in advance. The party can accept or refuse jobs, split up, negotiate, sneak, attack, retreat or invent a different answer.

entries.name: The World — ESTABLISHED
entries: The Free City of Bellweather was sold by its Council to the Crown while the party was at Kellan's Well. Every Council member, including Perrin Cardon, departed after the sale. The Council no longer governs.

King Hendrix Stucky rules from the capital. His son Prince Reginald Stucky and Reginald's wife Princess Narcia Stucky govern Bellweather. The royals are comically entitled and cruel, but the government has real power and coherent administrators.
Koven House is the Crown's municipal headquarters and records office. Ledger House remains independent and under Brakkus Ledgerhelm. Bishop Brann stayed in Bellweather.
Cardon Weavehouse is OWNED BY THE CROWN, despite its old name. Perrin has no current ownership claim. The Crown employs a coercive indentured labor system there.

Jaroood is a 243-year-old HIGH ELF who came to Bellweather with Prince Reginald. He has COMPLETE OPERATIONAL CONTROL of the Crown-owned Weavehouse: staff, shifts, discipline, worker assignments, admissions, debt assessments, records and releases. He believes the Crown's debt-based slavery is justified, personally earns 10% of EACH ADDITIONAL DEBT ASSESSMENT beyond a worker's original principal, and remains loyal because the Crown enriches and protects him. He fears only losing Crown favor. His voice is a younger, vigorous Mr. Burns, nasal and condescending without frailty. He stands 5 ft. 11 in., slender, with pale gold eyes, narrow face, slicked-back silver-blond hair, burgundy coat and ivory waistcoat.
Brakkus is a half-orc retired level-16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Oghma, not of any other god. His mother Elena was a librarian who taught him to read and understand people before judging them.
Bishop Brann proposed that the PCs outwardly cooperate with the Crown while secretly passing information to him and Brakkus. Opposition is beginning, not an already established spy organization.

The Radiant Well is a real magical phenomenon below the surface, relevant to the old legend Brakkus told about possible influence over minds. Its nature, access route, and any Crown connection are OPEN, not automatic campaign answers.

entries.name: Campaign Play Standard
entries: Give named NPCs established physical descriptions and reliable portrayal cues on their first appearance. Let them react according to beliefs, information and circumstances.
Preserve all established shop catalogs and the approved Bellweather Crown-era overview and Ledger House map.
Future chapter locations remain. Former events, enemy lineups, property disputes, treasure placements, villains, predetermined advancement and finales are not current canon.

entries.name: Historical Position
entries: The campaign opened with the storm and the adventurers' arrival around Bellweather. Ledger House became the party's home base.
The old playable encounter outline is archived. It does not imply every originally drafted beat occurred.

entries.name: Current Conditions
entries: Use the approved Crown-era Bellweather map, including the established South Ward, Maren Isle, surrounding geography and existing landmarks. Do not redraw its basic geography.
Crown authority operates through Koven House. Ledger House is independently run by Brakkus. Shops and citizens have their own lives and may have differing reactions to the takeover.
A building shown on an old map remains a location; its former proposed owners, occupants and encounter scripts do not.

entries.name: Established Outcomes
entries: The party freed seven captives: Nela Orr, Council surveyors Lessa Dorn and Kav Orin, three other temple caretakers and a wounded temple guard.
Tal Rusk and remaining opponents were killed; the recovered reliquary went to Bishop Brann. The coded ledger, spyglass and compass passed into Council custody before the Council departed.
The PCs reached level 4 after Blackstone.
The former Council sentenced Pepper for killing Kaleb to five service missions: Kellan's Well unpaid, four subsequent paid missions. That sentence has never been formally discharged.

entries.name: Session 4 — PLAYED / Authoritative
entries: After the Well, the party killed Noren and his Veteran. The Veteran was beheaded; Arunem carried the body in a bag. A city guard confirmed the Council was gone. The bag was repeatedly slammed to the ground; the precise actor and final whereabouts of the body are not recorded.
Pepper went alone to the market and had a bad encounter with Edda Pell, half-orc owner of The Spare Button, now voiced with an Irish accent. No specific new debt, injury or shop-ban was established.

Pepper voluntarily approached Koven House to report Edda. Royal guards recognized her in their records, asserted the Crown held her service contract and detained her for hard labor at the southern ruins.

Brakkus found and accompanied Jarrock and Aaron in seeking Pepper. He persuaded the guards to release Pepper into HIS custody. It was a negotiated release, not a jail break. Exact terms of the arrangement remain OPEN.

Bishop Brann told the party the Council sold Bellweather and departed; Brann did not take a payment from the Crown's acquisition. He proposed covert intelligence sharing while the group appeared to be cooperative Crown hires.
Brann paid outstanding Kellan's Well wages: Jarrock RECEIVED 100 gp, Aaron RECEIVED 100 gp, Arunem RECEIVED 100 gp, Pepper RECEIVED nothing. Do not pay those three shares twice.
Brakkus described an old legend of possible mind-affecting magic in Bellweather. Brakkus DOES NOT know the true existence or position of the Radiant Well. The party only heard the legend.

Tulcornix Avemvir, Kaleb's adopted aarakocra brother, sought help freeing his sister-in-law Elowen, Kaleb's widow, from Crown-controlled Weavehouse indenture. A different phonetic name in the session recap does not establish a second person.
At the table Elowen's alleged debt was stated as 150 gp principal, 200 gp administrative charges and 50 gp/day for room and board. Pepper offered all her money. No release or payment is confirmed.

Aaron stationed his familiar to watch the Weavehouse overnight. The party started planning a covert rescue. Brakkus advised stealth to protect their cover. The familiar's findings and the party's chosen method are not established.

entries.name: Session 5 — PREPARED
entries: Begin with the party's unresolved plan to free Elowen and with Aaron's familiar watching the site. Aim for a normal 3–3½-hour game without dictating how many minutes each choice takes.

Brakkus should have a conversation with Aaron. He knows Aaron is a dhampir and implied Oghma may have guided Aaron to Ledger House. This is Brakkus's belief or question, NOT confirmed divine intervention.
Brakkus follows his Oghma-informed interest in understanding Aaron rather than judging him by his lineage. Let Aaron's player decide what to share; do not force a grand revelation.

Let the party choose the approach to the Weavehouse, including a public petition, purchase, forged orders, infiltration, distraction, negotiation or combat. The Crown responds to what its people plausibly learn.
Brann and Brakkus have reasons to avoid attracting attention, but they are not the PCs' commanders. They continue their own lives.

entries.name: Session 5 — Morning at Ledger House (LOCKED PREP, unplayed)
entries: OPEN at Ledger House's approved ground-floor common room the morning after Aaron's familiar Drysa watched the Weavehouse overnight. Brakkus is tending the bar/breakfast. The party still intends to help Elowen. The four opening beats can overlap: Drysa reports; Elena introduces Detritus; Jord seeks a room and offers a hat; Brakkus privately asks Aaron about how he came to Bellweather. No new crisis or forced order of scenes.

READ ALOUD: 'Morning has come to Bellweather. Downstairs at Ledger House, breakfast is being served, guests trade news, and Brakkus is tending the bar. Outside, the city carries on under its new rulers. You've had the night to think about Elowen and the Weavehouse, and Drysa has been watching the building. You can now hear what she learned.'

The approved Ledger House map provides the common room/bar, porch for arrivals and back courtyard for a private conversation. An old shrine label on the physical map conflicts with the current god; its correct dedication is Oghma. Let the party decide timing of research, attunement, shopping, reconnaissance or raid.

entries.name: Drysa Overnight Watch — LOCKED Perception Result Script
entries: Drysa is Aaron's established pseudodragon familiar. The 2024 Pseudodragon has Wisdom (Perception) +5, Passive Perception 15, Stealth +4, Darkvision 60 ft. and Blindsight 10 ft. Austin rolls ONE d20+5 for the exterior watch; read all tiers achieved, cumulatively. No automatic interior exploration.

ALL ROLLS: 'Drysa observed a southern public entrance and a western loading entrance used for deliveries. The building became quieter after business hours. Most production lights went dark, but a light stayed on in the southern portion late into the night. Nobody seemed permanently stationed at either exterior entrance.'

15–19 ADD: 'A large, heavily built armed figure crossed the western loading approach, disappeared back into the building, and later returned. It appears to follow a patrol, rather than stand outside.' Describe its Bugbear identity only if her actual vantage/lighting could reveal it.
20–24 ADD: 'Drysa noticed the figure returned roughly every eight minutes. The brief interval just after it went back inside appears to be the best time to approach the loading area.'

25+ ADD: 'During the patrol cycles Drysa could observe, no other guard took the figure's position. From outside she saw a short interval without anyone watching the western door directly. Someone inside an unseen window or room could still be looking out.'

14 OR BELOW: base description only. Perception determines observed facts. Do not require Investigation just to understand the patrol pattern after observing it; use Intelligence (Investigation), suggested DC 13, only for an additional deduction supported by genuine clues.

NO RESULT discloses Room 19, Elowen, Jaroood, the monsters, master key, room numbers, or a guaranteed safe interior route. If Drysa was outside telepathic/senses-sharing range, she returns to Aaron to communicate the report; she did not give him unlimited live vision. A risky closer vantage only reveals what she can actually see and may call for Stealth +4.

entries.name: Detritus Arrival — LOCKED Introduction, Vision Still OPEN
entries: Elena plays Detritus, male Rock Gnome Wizard level 4, seeking a way to prevent his home being destroyed after a vision. The location of home, precise imagery, cause, origin, timeline, and character's wizard subclass/spells are NOT established. There is no automatic tie to the Crown, the Radiant Well or earlier villains.

Detritus arrives at Ledger House via the existing front porch seeking information in Bellweather. Marren Library is one plausible place he may ask about, but Elena defines what Detritus says and how he presents his journey. Ask Elena to describe his appearance rather than writing it for her.

Brakkus can answer ordinary local questions and introduce Detritus to the travelers he already knows: 'These folks have been around Bellweather more than most newcomers. They might know where to begin.' This does not disclose the group's covert plans. Detritus may offer help/companionship while searching for answers, and the players decide what to tell him and how to include him. Marren Library remains a possible future research stop, not a known solution to the vision.

entries.name: Brakkus and Aaron — LOCKED Private Dialogue
entries: Brakkus finds a quiet moment and invites Aaron into the EXISTING Ledger House back courtyard, or speaks later if Austin declines. He already knows Aaron is a dhampir. He does NOT automatically know Dimidicus's name, the mysterious liberator, Aaron's dreams or that Oghma intervened.
OPEN: 'Aaron, can I ask you something? What brought you to Bellweather? How did you find your way to my door?' Let Austin answer before continuing.

IF AARON DESCRIBES THE PULL OR DREAMS: 'I serve Oghma. I've wondered whether he had a hand in your finding this place. That's all it is, though: a suspicion. I don't have an answer.' Never confirm a divine action.

IF AARON ASKS ABOUT BEING DHAMPIR: 'I know. It hasn't changed your welcome here.' If he asks why: 'My father was a warlord. My mother was a librarian he kept captive. She taught me to read.' He may share further details if Aaron invites them. If Austin talks about his former master, Brakkus listens and may offer help researching the mystery without claiming prior knowledge.

IF AARON DOESN'T WANT TO TALK: 'Fair enough. My door's open if you change your mind.' Brakkus returns to ordinary inn business. The encounter is about understanding Aaron, not imposing a revelation or compulsory faith test.

entries.name: Jord's Lodging and Hat of Disguise — LOCKED Offer, NOT GIVEN YET
entries: Jord, established 86-year-old traveling gnome merchant with untidy sandy hair, spectacles and coat full of pockets, arrives with bags needing a room: the Crown took over his hotel for royal-guard barracks. His shop remains open, with its normal stock and already-promised 20% party discount.

The party previously recovered his horse and stolen strongbox; he already rewarded them. He is glad to see them at Ledger House, and may greet fellow gnome Detritus without assuming a prior friendship. He knows nothing about Tulcornix approaching the party or the Weavehouse rescue unless told.

Jord offers ONE personal {@item Hat of Disguise|XDMG} to the group as a GIFT out of goodwill for their past help and irritation at the Crown's commandeering of property. It is a personal possession, not a purchase or new wagon-stock item. Suggested voice line: 'You saved my horse and my strongbox. Reckon you can get better use out of this than I have. Here, take it.' Do not assign it to Aaron automatically.

If accepted in play, one party member may attune during a one-hour Short Rest. The Uncommon Hat of Disguise lets the attuned wearer cast {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} at will, an illusion lasting up to an hour and ending on removal. Standard attunement cap three; no instantaneous handoff between PCs. Until accepted, the hat is NOT in party inventory.
Edda Pell's separately stocked Hat of Disguise at The Spare Button is unaffected. Jord's normal inventory, prices, discount and prior reward stay as they were.

entries.name: Opening Branch Checks — LOCKED
entries: Party leaves before Jord's offer: they do not have the hat, but the raid is still playable. Receiving it doesn't bypass the required Short Rest. Drysa rolls low: basic exterior information still stands and further scouting is an actual new action, not a reroll of the night.

Detritus doesn't share the vision: he can still meet the party and seek local knowledge. Aaron declines a private talk: Brakkus stops without pressing. Party chooses a different destination: the world continues and the Weavehouse remains in its locked prepared state. Nothing here is retroactively PLAYED.

entries.name: The Crown and Unknowns
entries: King Hendrix is the reigning monarch. Reginald and his wife Narcia administer Bellweather. Council members including Cardon have departed. No former Councillor retains authority by default.
Koven House's public office accepts routine questions and petitions. Its existing map does not mandate the old unplayed garrison placement or a battle.
Brakkus's negotiated custody of Pepper is real, but its detailed enforcement documents, deadlines or other conditions are OPEN.
The Well's magical reality and subterranean nature are DM-only. The precise entrance, mechanism and Crown's interest are OPEN. No retired villain possesses it by default.

entries.name: Location Only — OPEN
entries: Savin Keep and its established location and maps remain available. Old reclamation orders, faction assignments, soldiers, treasure and outcomes have been retired.
Rebuild new events later from the Crown-era world and the party's choices.

entries.name: Authority / Occupation — ESTABLISHED
entries: The former Cardon Weavehouse is Crown-owned; Perrin Cardon left with the Council. No outstanding Cardon claim or ownership contest exists.

Jaroood, a 243-year-old HIGH ELF, arrived with Prince Reginald and has COMPLETE OPERATIONAL CONTROL of Crown-owned Cardon Weavehouse, including staff, workers, discipline, admissions, operations, debt assessments and release signatures. He believes the royal system of slavery is justified, is loyal to the Crown because it enriches him and fears its displeasure. His authorized personal commission is 10% of every new debt assessment beyond the original principal, credited when assessed. He is 5 ft. 11 in. tall, slender, with a narrow face, pale gold eyes, slicked-back silver-blond hair, immaculate burgundy coat and ivory waistcoat; voice: a more vigorous, younger Mr. Burns.
Elowen, Kaleb's widow, is an indentured textile worker. She wants her freedom and may speak for herself. She is not obligated to express gratitude or accept a particular solution.

The amount the party was told is 150 gp principal + 200 gp administrative charges + 50 gp per day room and board. This asserted price is not an ethical endorsement or a statement that any PC has already paid it.

entries.name: Jaroood — Complete NPC Dossier (DM Only, ESTABLISHED)
entries: {@b Identification.} Jaroood is a 243-year-old high elf, Medium Humanoid, lawful evil; his formal title is Royal Administrator of Cardon Weavehouse. He accompanied Prince Reginald from outside Bellweather. He is not Perrin Cardon's steward and has no ownership dispute to resolve.

{@b First description (read or paraphrase).} A slender high elf in a perfectly fitted burgundy coat stands behind a desk. His silver-blond hair is combed straight back from a narrow face; pale-gold eyes pass over you with brisk calculation. A heavy gold signet of the Crown sits on one long finger. He speaks in a refined, slightly nasal voice that makes even an insult sound like a courtesy.

{@b Voice and gestures.} Perform a younger and more vigorous Mr. Burns: nasal, soft, precise, delighted by profit, and condescending without shouting. He steeples his fingers when pleased, checks the edge of a ledger before replying, glances at a pocket watch when someone wastes time, and uses {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} to clean dust from his clothes after inspections. When royal authority is credible, he straightens and becomes swiftly deferential.

{@b Core belief.} He believes the Crown's indentured slavery is justified and worker hardship is a problem of individual indebtedness. He sincerely considers the provision of shelter, rations and supervision something for which the workers must be charged. His cruelty is casual, not theatrical rage.

{@b Motivation.} Make as much money as possible for as long as possible and remain protected by the Stucky Crown. His ambition is lasting wealth and security, not to rule Bellweather or replace the royals. He fears only the Crown's displeasure as a durable threat to his position.

{@b Authority.} Jaroood has COMPLETE OPERATIONAL CONTROL of the Crown-owned Weavehouse. He sets staffing, daily hours, work assignments, disciplinary policy, administrative charges, access to confined workers, and release procedures. The Hobgoblin Captain, the two other humanoid labor guards, the clerk, and his personal magical defenders act under his operational authority. He can sign a discharge himself when the account is settled or when he otherwise chooses to authorize it; there is no invented offsite owner who must countersign. Actual royal orders outrank his position.

{@b Authorized commission.} He receives 10% of each ADDITIONAL debt amount ASSESSED against an indentured worker beyond the initial principal. It is an explicit part of his Crown-approved compensation, not secret embezzlement. The remaining assessed sums belong to Crown accounts. His entitlement is credited when the charge is assessed, not only when the worker pays; administrative pay is settled periodically through Crown accounting. He may propose or authorize new charges under his broad authority, but his books must account for them.

{@b Elowen example (NO RETCON OF DAY COUNT).} The party heard 150 gp original debt, 200 gp administrative fees and 50 gp per day for room/board. Her claimed outstanding balance after d charged days is 350 + 50d gp, before any actual credits or new assessed charges. Jaroood's commission credited on those additions is 20 + 5d gp. He receives no 10% commission on the original 150 gp. No number of elapsed days or additional fees has yet been established.

{@b Office routine.} At the beginning of the workday he checks admissions, overdue accounts and charge entries from his clerks. During the morning he inspects output and labor assignments, taking an interest in missed quotas. Through the afternoon he hears petitions and approves charges, transfers and discharges. Near closing he signs the day ledger and has totals prepared for the Crown. He remains in an administrative office within the existing Weavehouse layout; its exact room should be keyed when the map is reconciled. He is not automatically visible at the public counter or outside overnight.

{@b Private possessions.} He carries a signet ring used on official release papers, a gold pocket watch, and an immaculate personal pocket ledger with commission calculations. The Crown's labor ledger is an official work record held by the clerk, separate from his own convenient private notes. His clothes and these objects are not magic items; no hidden treasure cache is introduced.

{@b What he knows.} He knows how the annex works, the identities of workers admitted under his control, their accounts, and the authority delegated to him by the Crown. He does not automatically know the party's covert role, Aaron's familiar, Brakkus's private conversations, the Crown's unexplained wider plans or the Radiant Well.

{@b Workers and security.} Workers receive work orders through Jaroood, his clerk, and three humanoid labor guards: a Hobgoblin Captain, a Hobgoblin Warrior and a Bugbear Warrior. These guards handle headcounts, doors, discipline and escape prevention rather than waiting to fight the party. A {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, {@creature Mimic|XMM} and {@creature Earth Elemental|XMM} protect Jaroood in his private rooms. They do not automatically attack ordinary visitors under guard supervision. He is civil to guests who can pay, useful to powerful people, and dismissive of workers. He relies on Crown authority and procedural control, not personal combat prowess.

{@b When approached about Elowen.} He looks up her account and quotes the amount honestly recorded at that moment; no surprise mandatory release fee is imposed just to thwart a player solution. He prefers prolonging indebtedness but will consider immediate full payment or terms that earn him profit. Because he controls discharge procedures, he may sign a legitimate release himself. Elowen still speaks for herself.

{@b Bargaining.} A plea to his conscience will not sway him. An offer that improves his income or protects him from blame may. Straightforward public business needs no roll. A plausible claim of royal authority or forged release warrants scrutiny, with a suggested DC 15 Charisma (Deception) check if a roll is needed; corroborating credible documents or good preparation can make the check easier or unnecessary. Real orders from the prince supersede him.

{@b How to pressure him.} Revealing his 10% commission alone does NOT threaten him: the Crown authorizes it. Evidence that he falsely reports Crown proceeds, harms an important royal interest, or knowingly disobeys a valid order WOULD endanger his status, but none of those forms of misconduct are pre-established discoveries. Players must earn or create leverage.

{@b Under violence.} Jaroood is an administrator, not a heroic duelist. He relies on his Gargoyle, Mimic and Earth Elemental if present, retreats, and uses his high elf {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} to escape an immediate physical threat if possible. Do not invent extra guards or a hidden strike team. He can surrender, bargain or be overcome. Witnesses and paperwork, not an infinite combat roster, determine later Crown consequences.

{@b On success or failure.} If the party gains Elowen's lawful release, he makes the entry, sends the clerk to update records, and resumes profitable operations. If she is secretly extracted, he first reconciles headcount and records, then pursues credible institutional reporting; he is not omniscient. His concern is protecting himself and his earnings.

{@b Suggested lines.} 'Slavery? No, no. A structured opportunity to settle one's obligations.' / 'You cannot expect accommodations to pay for themselves.' / 'How gratifying. Another account adjusted upward.' / 'His Highness has ordered it? Naturally, that changes everything.'

{@b At-the-table stat block.} {@creature Jaroood|NCFA} is based on the 2024 Noble in physical threat level, with high elf magic. His defense is the institution. See his dedicated monster entry; he is not designed as a boss encounter.

{@b Primordial (Terran) and personal-defense trigger — APPROVED.} He speaks Common, Elvish and Primordial (Terran), and uses Terran to command the Gargoyle and Earth Elemental. The Elemental does not attack solely from Tremorsense. Saying 'Defend your master' in Terran OR an attack on Jaroood or the Elemental in Room 19, provided the Elemental actually perceives the impact, injury, magical effect or resulting commotion using its own senses, even if it cannot see the attacker triggers its defense. The Mimic responds to prey/threats, not his Terran speech.

{@b Mechanical alarm and worker keys — APPROVED.} Jaroood has a simple mechanical bell pull in Room 19, connected by a rope and overhead pulleys to the bell INSIDE Room 11 only. Its exposed stretch can be cut or unhooked in the corridor outside his suite before entry. No electricity or citywide message. He carries a master key opening all four worker sleeping rooms, one action per door. His labor guards are instructed to capture, NEVER kill, fleeing worker assets.

entries.name: Approved Map Re-Key — All Numbered Rooms (LOCKED Session 5 Prep, Not Played)
entries: Keep the actual approved DM and player Weavehouse maps. Room numbers below assign functions to existing spaces but DO NOT add doors, windows, external exits, walls or secret passages. If a label is not printed on a specific copy, treat the corresponding item as a functional area of the nearest suitable existing space rather than inventing a new numbered room.
1. Timekeeper and attendance desk: Daytime clerk checks work hours and labor slips.
2. Public receiving/check-in: Petitions and escorted visitors are directed from here.
3. Wool inspection: Raw fleece is counted and graded.
4. North weaving floor: Active looms by day, empty production area overnight.
5. Thread and dye ingredients: Locked consumable store, not a secret treasure room.
6. Finished cloth inventory: Counted bales awaiting dispatch.
7. North store closet: Routine tools and wrapping supplies.
8. Western service passage: Bugbear's regular patrol circuit, not a guard room.
9. Worker sleeping room A: Four workers; locked after headcount.
10. Worker sleeping room B: Four workers; locked after headcount.
11. Chief overseer's office: Hobgoblin Captain's desk, central roster, spare worker keys, reporting bell.
12. Clerk files and supplies: Routine records and work orders if the printed room is numbered 12.
13. Dyeing/pressing workroom: Workers during day, generally quiet at night.
14. Eastern service passage: Circulation to rooms on the east side.
15. Main production hall: Large floor and loom machinery; Earth Elemental works here during daytime only.
16. Cloth finishing and packing: Packed stock, bales and ordinary supplies.
17. Worker sleeping room C: Five workers; locked after headcount.
18. Worker sleeping room D: Four workers; locked after headcount.
19. Jaroood's private accounting and residential suite: Jaroood and Elowen kept together; Gargoyle, Mimic and, after shift, Earth Elemental.
20. Jaroood's private secure filing room: Personal account records, stationery, sealed releases and correspondence; access through EXISTING passages.
21. Western receiving/loading point: Service approach and a potential escape route only through actual drawn doors.
22. Raw-material storage: Cotton and wool bundles, not prisoners.
23. South public approach and reception: Visitor traffic and front-facing circulation, using the actual mapped access.
24. Dispatch/staging: Outgoing cloth and bundles.
25. Eastern storage and housekeeping: Cleaning and service goods, not extra staff or guards.

The existing map is authoritative over any prose claim about connectivity. Use only mapped routes for combat, patrols and evacuation. Jaroood's private suite is room 19 because it already depicts more elaborate interior furnishings and accommodates a personal confrontation. The much larger room 15 comfortably suits heavy labor. Room 11 is near an internal junction for captain oversight.
Physical furniture shown on the map stays; additional bedding, fabric, account papers, simple service equipment and guarding figures are movable contents, not renovations.

entries.name: Population, Positions and Daily Routine — LOCKED Session 5 Prep
entries: WORKFORCE — LOCKED SESSION 5 PREP: 18 indentured workers, including Elowen. Four are in room 9, four in room 10, five in room 17 and four in room 18 (17 ordinary workers), all kept under guard and locked into their assigned rooms after evening count. Elowen is NOT in a shared dormitory; she is compelled to serve and remain close to Jaroood in private room 19, with a cot behind a screen. Her personal service is domestic/clerical work, not evidence of any unestablished abuse. Lock 18 as the prepared session count until the DM expressly revises it. Not a number already observed by the players.

LABOR SECURITY: exactly three speaking, thinking, witness-capable overseers, not generic veteran/scout extras: {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM} (chief overseer), {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM} (quarters sentry), {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM} (patrolling escape catcher). They keep workers confined, supervise shifts and respond to escape attempts. The one civilian clerk works in reception and with the Captain; no extra guard squad waits off-map.

CAPTAIN: primarily at Room 11 with shift ledger, backup keys and the ONLY interior alarm bell. On isolated unexplained noises, sends or allows a single guard to investigate; if alarm or escape is verified, coordinates worker containment. He does NOT automatically abandon the workforce to rescue Jaroood.

WARRIOR: stationed near access to Rooms 9–10 and checks Rooms 17–18 during headcount. Carries practical worker-room keys; at night leaves standing position briefly for hourly inspection. If an escape or alarm is discovered, prioritizes keeping remaining quarters locked and captures workers nonlethally. Does not abandon all prisoners to rush into Jaroood's private fight.

BUGBEAR: patrols approximately every eight minutes along the existing western/southern corridors, especially near Room 8, Room 21 loading and Rooms 17–18. When a minor noise has no obvious culprit, he investigates alone along a real route, looks briefly and returns with a dismissive 'Must be the wind.' Actual evidence of a breakout or intruders prompts real action and a report. He prefers capturing escaping workers without lethal force. Never invent a shortcut across walls to complete his patrol.
THE CLERK: handles ordinary visitors at rooms 2 and 11 during office hours, then departs after close. He knows names only if actually given or recorded. Do not place him automatically overnight.

ELOWEN: serves and stays in room 19 with Jaroood in the evening and overnight. Jaroood conducts private accounting and takes his four-hour elf trance there; her sleeping place is screened within the same existing room. During working hours she attends Jaroood when he moves about the administrative rooms. She is not placed elsewhere to force a scripted confrontation.

PRIVATE SECURITY: by day {@creature Earth Elemental|XMM} works or stands ready in Room 15, moving along real passages to Room 19 after production closes. In Room 19 its 60-foot Tremorsense lets it sense movement but DOES NOT itself activate security action. It fights only on Jaroood's Terran command 'Defend your master' or if an attack on Jaroood or the Elemental in Room 19, provided the Elemental actually perceives the impact, injury, magical effect or resulting commotion using its own senses, even if it cannot see the attacker. The {@creature Gargoyle|XMM} stands motionless as decorative stonework and protects Jaroood in response to actual threats or his Terran command. The {@creature Mimic|XMM} occupies a gilded coffer or cabinet and attacks threats or prey based on its animalistic awareness and learned routine, not understanding Common-language orders. These three are the entirety of his personal monstrous security. This is a separate defense trigger; no hostility based solely on detected footsteps.

JAROOOD: room 19 is the reliable after-hours location for both him and Elowen; room 20 holds private records. If a PC legitimately observes him leave, reflect that new fact, but do not relocate him offscreen simply to block a clever plan. He has his personal signet, pocket ledger and accessible workhouse master keys unless play establishes otherwise.

DAY SHIFT: weaving, receiving and inspections operate until evening. NIGHT: the production rooms empty, 17 workers are locked into rooms 9,10,17,18, clerk has departed, three humanoid guards maintain security, and Jaroood + Elowen + personal defenders are in room 19. The familiar watched the previous night, so its report may illuminate exterior patterns but not the entire interior schedule.

entries.name: Approach, Patrols, Doors, Familiar and Alarms — LOCKED Session 5 Prep
entries: Aaron's familiar has had a full night outside. Describe only visible exterior entrances, windows that are actually visible, guard changes, the Bugbear's external movements if it passed a visible opening, and the difference between busy day/quiet night. It does not know numbered rooms, interior monsters or Jaroood's private suite without actual line of sight. Its shape and exact viewing post control findings.

Use existing mapped west-side service/loading access near area 21 and the southern public approach around area 23 for plausible approach choices only insofar as actual exterior openings are printed. Do not create a new side door. A legitimate public approach by day needs no Stealth check. The after-hours service lock is DC 15 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) if reachable.

Approaching room 19 using the mapped southern/interior corridors should allow a route around room 11 and the main industrial floor, if PCs identify and exploit it. Verify actual doors on the DM map at the table; there is no invisible secret corridor. A distracted guard can create an opening, and moving through unseen spaces shouldn't require meaningless group Stealth rolls.

EARTH ELEMENTAL SENSING AND TRIGGER — APPROVED. Its 60-foot Tremorsense pinpoints movement touching a continuous surface but cannot reveal identities or intentions. It NEVER activates, pursues, sounds an alarm, or reports someone solely because it senses footsteps, including unrecognized footsteps. It has ONE separately defined combat trigger: either Jaroood deliberately commands 'Defend your master' in Primordial (Terran), or an attack on Jaroood or the Elemental in Room 19, provided the Elemental actually perceives the impact, injury, magical effect or resulting commotion using its own senses, even if it cannot see the attacker (including a blow that instantly kills Jaroood, provided the Elemental notices its effects). Once triggered it acts according to the published {@creature Earth Elemental|XMM} stat block and Jaroood's standing orders to protect the suite. If both threats and orders cease, it remains at its post rather than patrolling after unrelated noises. Its sensing is not the same as triggering. Seeing the attacker is not required; perceiving the attack's effects is. If the attack and aftermath are genuinely imperceptible to the Elemental, it does not automatically activate. An attack heard or sensed through the connected floor may count if it creates unmistakable evidence, not if it produces ordinary footsteps alone.

ALARM — APPROVED. The alarm is a mundane rope-and-pulley BELL-PULL, not electricity, telegraph wire, a spell, or magical transmission. A pull cord beside Jaroood's desk in Room 19 runs through eyelets on the EXISTING corridor's upper wall/ceiling to a brass bell at the Room 11 overseer station. An exposed service-length of the SAME rope can be spotted and reached in the corridor just outside Room 19, with no new passage, room, or wall opening. Quietly unhook/disable without obvious damage: DC 13 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) if needed; a PC who reaches the exposed rope can simply sever it as an action (AC 12, 5 HP if attacked in combat). The alarm bell sounds ONLY INSIDE THE WEAVEHOUSE; it has no outside bell, magical relay or Crown-wide notification. A live guard at Room 11 learns an alarm was pulled, not who pulled it or why. Guards outside that room may hear the bell if sound can reach them through normal interior passages; no person outside the facility receives the alarm. Other independent noise (shouts, open doors, thunder magic, collapsing walls) can still be heard normally.

Private rooms have substantial doors, but no magic soundproofing. If players shut them, ordinary conversation/brief fighting may be muffled; a sustained roaring battle, spell that makes a loud bang, someone escaping into a hallway, or the Elemental breaking masonry may attract investigation. Decide audible consequences from actual distance, walls and timing, not a fixed alarm clock.

An ordinary dormitory lock is DC 15 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) or a matching guard/master key. Every dormitory must be opened separately, but do not create four separate skill checks if a master key fits them all. Exits shown on the map can be opened from inside by basic manual latches once reached; workers do not need an escort to operate them if they are not physically guarded.

The Hat of Disguise is only an available tool if Jord actually loans it and a single PC attunes. It conceals only its attuned wearer's appearance, not all five people. The Crown knows nothing about Tulcornix having approached the party.

SUSPICIOUS NOISE RESPONSE — APPROVED. On an isolated scrape, a dropped item or muffled thump with NO alarm and NO clear evidence of an intruder, send ONE nearby free guard to investigate by normal mapped travel, usually the Bugbear if he is on patrol. He checks the source area, spends a round or two looking for visible evidence, and, finding none, mutters something like 'Must be the wind' and returns to his previously assigned route. He does not summon everyone, magically know the PCs are there, or remain permanently on high alert after a single inconclusive noise. If he actually sees an unauthorized creature, opened cell, fleeing worker, incapacitated colleague, damaged lock or other convincing evidence, he responds appropriately and may report it. Repeated clearly related noises or obvious sustained combat are not hand-waved away.

ALARM OR MASS BREAKOUT RESPONSE — APPROVED. On a genuine pulled alarm the Captain at Room 11 takes charge and gives a normal shouted/running order to any guard he can contact; the bell is not an outside alert. The Hobgoblin Warrior immediately secures unbreached worker doors and blocks movement at the nearest actual corridor; the Bugbear moves to capture escapees or chase an observed intruder, whichever prevents the most loss of workers; the Captain manages keys, posts and information and joins an action only when he has real evidence and a real route. The three guards PRIORITIZE keeping indentured workers in Crown custody, because worker debts produce Crown/Jaroood income. They do NOT automatically all abandon prisoners to help Jaroood in Room 19. If the guards discover a breakout without the alarm, use the same responses only after the discovery has been communicated or witnessed.

NONLETHAL LABOR GUARD ORDERS — APPROVED. All indentured workers are Crown assets. Guards are explicitly FORBIDDEN to use lethal force against escaping workers. Against them, use grapples, Shoves, blocking exits, manacles, nets where available, and nonlethal finishing melee attacks under 2024 rules; no deliberate lethal arrow fire or lethal spell against a worker. If a worker escapes, the guard pursues or secures remaining workers rather than killing an asset to prevent escape. Armed intruders threatening guards are not treated as Crown assets and can be fought lethally. Incidental collateral danger still exists and should be adjudicated normally.

MASTER KEY / RELEASE SEQUENCE — APPROVED. Jaroood's workhouse master key opens all FOUR worker dormitory locks in Rooms 9, 10, 17 and 18. Unlocking and opening EACH door takes ONE action by a creature with the key, without a check; four doors take four actions in total, which may be split among characters only if they have additional valid keys or independently pick locks. The Hobgoblin Warrior has quarters keys and the Captain keeps backups. Without keys, ordinary lock-picking takes DC 15 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools) and an action per door if combat time matters. As soon as a room opens its occupants run off independently toward a physically available exit, without waiting for other dormitories; the escape is not held until everyone is released. The party does not escort them. Their movement creates noise and evidence, and guards react only when they see/hear it or receive a report. If a door to an exit is still guarded, workers try other plausible routes; the three guards can't stop every fleeing worker in all directions at once.

SUSTAINED COMBAT NOISE — LOCKED PREP: One unexplained scrape, clatter or isolated thump with no corroborating evidence gets ONE investigating guard, who returns to patrol with 'Must be the wind' if nothing is found. Repeated heavy impacts over consecutive rounds, sustained shouting, a door smashing, or conspicuous combat/spell noise are NOT dismissible as wind. ONE nearby guard initially investigates persistently by real mapped routes and actual movement time. If he discovers clear evidence (intruders, broken door, active fighting, escaping workers), he responds and attempts ordinary audible or face-to-face reporting to the Captain. Captain and Warrior prioritize containing worker assets and do not instantly teleport to Room 19. The bell still alerts only inside the facility, and an unobserved attacker is not magically identified.

entries.name: Private Confrontation — Room 19 (LOCKED Session 5 Prep)
entries: Jaroood is in room 19 with Elowen present, private records at hand. His office's decorative Gargoyle, disguised Mimic and visible stone Earth Elemental are all physically able to defend him when combat actually starts. The elemental is not merely a delayed encounter invented for difficulty, nor magically teleporting from room 15.

ROOM 19 VERTICAL DIMENSION — LOCKED PREP: The existing suite has a 15-foot ceiling above its current furniture, giving the Gargoyle room to use its published flight. This sets HEIGHT only; no changes to approved floor-plan walls, door locations or passages, and no new loft, upper floor or secret opening. Existing furniture and actual doorways still limit movement.

Jaroood keeps his published campaign NPC stats AC 15 / 9 HP. If Aaron or another PC kills him in one blow, he dies; don't inflate his HP or invent an escape. Elowen may move, hide or flee based on her interests. No script demands that she praise the party or stay in a combat zone.

The Gargoyle is a mobile protector understanding Primordial (Terran), which Jaroood speaks; it reacts to clear threats or a command. The Mimic attacks when genuinely disturbed or when violence brings prey/threats to its area; it is NOT a talking servant, and cannot identify intruders to future investigators. The Earth Elemental does NOT attack merely because Tremorsense pinpoints nearby footsteps. Its separate triggers are Jaroood's deliberate Terran command ('Defend your master') OR an attack on Jaroood or the Elemental in Room 19, provided the Elemental actually perceives the impact, injury, magical effect or resulting commotion using its own senses, even if it cannot see the attacker, even if the attack kills Jaroood immediately. After a trigger it uses its full published actions; it follows the mapped routes and cannot Earth Glide through worked walls.

The party could infiltrate, bluff, steal the signet/keys, isolate and bypass some personal defenders, capture Jaroood, negotiate a discharge or fight all three. In an upfront fight the three published creatures and Jaroood total 2,725 XP with 281 combined HP, a meaningful challenge for the five optimized level-4 PCs. Exact lethality/duration cannot be guaranteed without current character sheets.

The three ordinary labor guards join the personal confrontation only if they actually learn of it, can arrive by the existing mapped passages, and have secured or delegated their primary duty of retaining worker assets. An alarm pulls them into an organized labor-security response first, not an automatic rush into the suite; a mass escape especially keeps them busy with nonlethal recapture.

Stealth's reward is control of approach, avoiding those three ordinary guards, potential surprise/positioning, muted alarm, disguises and ability to free all workers afterward without recognizable witnesses. Do not add custom weak points to published creatures just to force a puzzle.

entries.name: Mass Liberation, Escape and Evidence — LOCKED Session 5 Prep
entries: Once the party uses Jaroood's master key (or another valid key) on each of Rooms 9, 10, 17 and 18, it takes one action per door to unlock/open. The 4, 4, 5 and 4 workers in those rooms immediately scatter on their own through the building's existing accessible exits; they do NOT wait for a coordinated escort. NO eighteen-person marching order, destination assignment, hiding plan or group Stealth roll is required. Real guards can catch individual fleeing workers with grapples and nonlethal force but cannot deliberately kill them, since they are income-producing Crown assets. They may chase the first group while other doors open, creating a genuine timing tradeoff.

If all 17 sleeping-room workers flee alongside Elowen, all 18 are free. If some rooms remain locked, the people there remain imprisoned. The party may free dormitories before confronting Jaroood, but the early movement of workers increases the chance that ordinary guards alert Jaroood and his defenders. World reacts to observed events only.

Mass escape brings official investigation and urgent guard duties. Officers know Jaroood died if his body is found and workers escaped if the count is wrong; neither fact inherently reveals the adventurers' names. No Crown official presently knows that Tulcornix approached or spoke to the party, and NO connection from Tulcornix to the party exists in Crown knowledge.

The humanoid guards can identify people they genuinely see, especially undisguised PCs; the Mimic and Elemental cannot give ordinary testimony; a surviving Gargoyle may be able to communicate what it saw. The Crown can later follow independent evidence, documents and genuine testimony, but do not automatically brand the party criminals.

The Crown still asserts the worker debts after physical escape. Destroyed local paperwork may impede immediate enforcement but does not retroactively establish that all debts have been legally canceled or that certified offsite copies exist. Jaroood's death doesn't erase his fees.

Scenario checks: (A) covert approach to Room 19, cut corridor bell rope, defeat protectors, take Jaroood's master key and unlock each of four dorms with one action apiece; as each opens, workers flee and guards react to genuine discovery; (B) premature mass breakout alerts guards to secure workers, and Jaroood may prepare or move Elowen; (C) isolated clatter causes ONE guard to briefly inspect and return to patrol if no evidence ('Must be the wind'); (D) direct public assault or clearly recognizable intruders creates credible identification; (E) forged/legal discharge or social plan can avoid combat; (F) Jaroood killed instantly before speaking Terran still triggers the elemental when it perceives the attack; Tremorsense by itself NEVER starts combat; (G) no outside Crown authority is automatically alerted by the indoor alarm.

Five level-4 PCs: Pepper (Cristian, Human Cleric), Jarrock (Emmi, Dragonborn Rogue), Aaron (Austin, Dhampir Fighter 1/Warlock 3), Arunem (Kiersten, Kalashtar Path of the World Tree Barbarian 4), and Detritus (Elena, Rock Gnome Wizard 4). The party is offensively optimized; do not treat standard XP budgeting as a reliable combat forecast.

entries.name: Weavehouse — LOCKED Session 5 DM Quick Reference
entries: STATUS: LOCKED SESSION 5 PREP, NOT PLAYED. Retain approved Weavehouse map and numbered room assignments. Population is 18 indentured workers including Elowen. Preserve Jaroood's 9 HP, the three speaking labor guards (Hobgoblin Captain, Hobgoblin Warrior, Bugbear Warrior) and three published personal defenders (Gargoyle, Mimic, Earth Elemental). No hidden guard waves.

ROOM 19: Jaroood and personal-servant Elowen occupy the private suite with Gargoyle, Mimic, and nighttime Earth Elemental. Ceiling is 15 feet high. This does not alter the walls, doors or approved map.

ALARM: A purely mechanical pull-rope connects Room 19 to a bell in Room 11, INSIDE Weavehouse ONLY. An exposed corridor segment outside Room 19 allows stealth sabotage (DC 13 Thieves' Tools to unhook quietly, or an action to cut). Guards outside the building are not automatically alerted.

NOISE: One uncertain sound summons ONE guard (usually Bugbear) who says 'Must be the wind' and resumes patrol if no evidence is found. Sustained clear combat makes that one guard keep investigating and report concrete findings by ordinary means. No automatic omniscient alert.

ELEMENTAL: Tremorsense alone never triggers it. Triggered by Jaroood's command in Primordial (Terran), or an actual attack on Jaroood/Elemental whose effects it perceives even if the attacker is hidden. An entirely unperceived strike does not magically trigger it. Gargoyle reacts to real threats/Terran orders; Mimic to prey and violence in its space.

WORKER GUARDS: Their job is containing labor assets and preserving Crown income. Alarm or discovered breakout: Captain coordinates, Warrior secures remaining quarters, Bugbear pursues escapees. They MUST capture workers nonlethally, but may fight armed attackers lethally. They join the private fight only if they know enough to respond and can get there without abandoning containment.

RELEASE: Jaroood's master key opens all four room locks (Rooms 9, 10, 17, 18), one action per room. Released workers run independently as their room opens; no escort, no shared Stealth check. The 17 ordinary workers plus Elowen total 18.

INVESTIGATION: A dead administrator and escaped workers prompt an investigation, not automatic identity recognition. The Crown does NOT know Tulcornix approached the party. Only evidence and genuine witnesses can produce identification.

SESSION INTEGRATION: The Hat of Disguise is not actually given until Jord does it in play. Detritus joining and the Brakkus/Aaron exchange are separate Session 5 prep. Do not script the party into one approach.

entries.name: Brakkus Ledgerhelm
entries: About 48, half-orc, level-16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Oghma. Retired by choice, proprietor of Ledger House, protective of people in his care.

Father: Korgak, Ironfang warlord. Mother: Elena, a captive human librarian who taught Brakkus literacy, knowledge and human dignity. After her death he rejected his father's legacy and took the surname Ledgerhelm.
Mentor: High Justiciar Vance Halford. Vance gave him the magic sword Brakkus named The Appendix.
Brakkus's faith was Oghma when played at Hall of Heroes, and remains Oghma in NCFA. He knows Aaron is a dhampir and seeks to understand him.
He negotiated Pepper's release into custody and is a credible independent civic actor. He is not a required field companion or solution to player obstacles.

For Session 5, privately ask Aaron what drew him to Bellweather and Ledger House. Brakkus knows he's dhampir but has no confirmed knowledge of his liberator or divine intervention. His possible Oghma role is speculation, not fact.

entries.name: Royal Administration
entries: King Hendrix Stucky reigns from outside Bellweather. Prince Reginald Stucky governs with his wife Princess Narcia Stucky. Their choices have consequences even if their manners are ridiculous.

Jaroood is a 243-year-old HIGH ELF and the Crown's absolute operational administrator at Cardon Weavehouse. He accompanied Prince Reginald to Bellweather, believes debt slavery justified and profits from it through a 10% Crown-approved commission on additional debts ASSESSED against each worker beyond original principal. His authority covers personnel, work, discipline, fee assessment and discharges. He fears losing Crown favor, not the workers' suffering. His young-Mr.-Burns voice is refined, nasal and condescending. He has pale-gold eyes, silver-blond hair and immaculate burgundy and ivory dress.
Perrin Cardon departed with the former Council and has no continuing ownership of the Weavehouse.

243-year-old high elf, 5 ft. 11 in., slender, pale gold eyes, silver-blond slicked-back hair, burgundy coat, ivory waistcoat and Crown signet. Younger, more vigorous Mr. Burns voice; steeples fingers and uses Prestidigitation to clean lint after inspections.

He controls personnel, discipline, assignments, assessments, and releases at the Crown-owned Weavehouse. He receives a Crown-authorized 10% commission on debt ADDED beyond original principal for every worker, credited as assessed, not based on actual repayment. Elowen's stated 200 gp fee yields him 20 gp; every 50 gp/day charge yields 5 gp per day. No days assumed.
High elf magic and combat stats are in {@creature Jaroood|NCFA}. He is an administrator, and his commission is not illicit from the Crown's viewpoint; disclosing it alone cannot blackmail him.

Elowen is Kaleb's widow and a Crown-confined textile worker. Her stated debt is in Chapter 8, and her future is not predetermined.

data.name: Appendix G: Generic DM Quick Reference

entries.name: Generic DCs
entries: Use these values when the adventure does not specify a DC. Choose the ability and skill from the character's approach. If success is automatic or impossible, do not call for a roll.

entries.name: Object and Material ACs and HP
entries: Use AC to determine whether an attack damages an unattended object. HP represents how much punishment the object can take before it breaks. In the core object rules, material primarily determines AC while size and whether the construction is fragile or resilient determine HP; the values below combine those rules into a fast DM reference.

The HP columns assume a typical fragile build for cloth/paper/rope and crystal/glass/ice, and a typical resilient build for wood/bone, stone, metal, mithral, and adamantine. Use a lower HP category for thin, rotten, cracked, or poorly made objects and a higher one for unusually thick or reinforced construction. For walls, gates, vehicles, and other very large structures, treat the attacked portion as a separate object and consider a damage threshold when appropriate.

entries.caption: Object AC and Typical HP by Material
Object HP by Size and Construction
Light and Obscurement
rows: Lightly Obscured; Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
Heavily Obscured; a creature effectively has the Blinded condition when trying to see into it.
Within its range, treat Dim Light as Bright Light and Darkness as Dim Light; colors in Darkness appear only as shades of gray.
Within its range, perceive without normal sight, including through Darkness and against Invisible creatures, unless blocked by Total Cover.
Within its range, see through normal and magical Darkness, see Invisible creatures, and automatically pierce visual illusions as specified by the sense.

rows: Can't see; automatically fails sight-dependent checks; attacks against the creature have Advantage, and its attacks have Disadvantage.
Can't attack the charmer or target it with harmful effects; the charmer has Advantage on social checks involving the creature.

Normally can't be targeted by effects requiring sight; Advantage on own attacks and Disadvantage on attacks against it unless the attacker can see it; Advantage on Initiative.
Incapacitated; Speed 0; automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against it have Advantage; qualifying close-range hits can become critical hits.

entries.name: Falling
entries: A creature takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet fallen, to a maximum of 20d6, and lands Prone unless an effect says otherwise.

entries.name: Jumping

entries.caption: Jumping Quick Reference
rows: Up to Strength score in feet

entries: Each foot jumped costs 1 foot of movement. Landing in Difficult Terrain after a Long Jump requires a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or the jumper becomes Prone. At the DM's option, clearing a low obstacle during a Long Jump can require a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. A creature can reach upward an additional distance equal to half its height during a High Jump.

items: {@b Use common sense.} An attack that cannot reasonably damage an object deals no meaningful damage regardless of the attack roll.

{@b Damage Threshold.} If an object has a damage threshold, damage from a single attack or effect below that threshold deals 0 damage; meeting or exceeding the threshold allows the full damage through.
{@b Damage Types.} Objects are generally immune to Poison and Psychic damage. Assign additional resistances, vulnerabilities, or immunities when the material makes them obvious.
{@b Huge and Gargantuan Objects.} Divide very large structures into Large or smaller sections and track damage to the relevant section rather than treating an entire building as one object.
{@b Automatic Breakage.} If an object is extremely fragile and the method is appropriate, allow it to be broken without rolling.

entries.name: Improvised Damage
entries: Use this when the environment causes damage and no specific rule gives a value. Choose the damage amount that best matches the severity of the event rather than the source's physical size alone.

entries.caption: Improvised Damage Examples
rows: Minor but meaningful hazard, such as hot coals or a heavy object falling onto someone.
Serious hazard, such as a lightning strike or falling into a firepit.
Severe hazard, such as collapsing rubble or falling into a vat of acid.
Extreme hazard, such as crushing machinery or moving through lava.
Catastrophic hazard, such as being submerged in lava or struck by a massive crashing structure.
Near-apocalyptic force appropriate to exceptionally destructive supernatural or colossal events.

entries.name: Common Improvised DC Examples
entries: These are generic examples, not fixed DCs. Adjust for tools, leverage, time pressure, conditions, and the character's approach.

entries.caption: Improvised DC Examples
rows: Climb a knotted rope with good footing; notice something obvious while actively searching.
Force a weak interior door; climb a rough wall with ample handholds; calm a mildly agitated animal.
Pick an ordinary lock; climb a wet or awkward surface; spot a reasonably concealed compartment; recall specialized lore.
Force a reinforced door; detect a carefully hidden feature; perform a difficult physical maneuver under pressure.
Defeat exceptional mundane security; accomplish a feat demanding rare expertise or strength.
Accomplish a legendary but still physically possible feat without magical assistance.

entries.name: Exhaustion
entries: Exhaustion is cumulative from level 1 through 6. A creature dies when it reaches Exhaustion level 6. Finishing a Long Rest normally removes 1 Exhaustion level.

entries.caption: Common Environmental Hazards
rows: A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each turn until the fire is extinguished, doused, submerged, or suffocated.
At 0°F or below, make a DC 10 Constitution save each hour or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance or Immunity automatically succeeds.

At 100°F or above without drinkable water, make an hourly Constitution save: DC 5 for the first hour, +1 per additional hour. Medium/Heavy armor gives Disadvantage; Fire Resistance or Immunity automatically succeeds.

After a number of minutes equal to Constitution score, make a DC 10 Constitution save each additional minute or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance/Immunity or natural adaptation automatically succeeds.
After each hour swimming deeper than 100 feet, a creature without a Swim Speed makes a DC 10 Constitution save or gains 1 Exhaustion level.
Difficult Terrain; entering it for the first time on a turn or starting there requires a DC 10 Dexterity save or the creature becomes Prone.
Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks; extinguishes open flames and disperses fog; flying creatures generally must land by the end of their turn or fall.
Area is Lightly Obscured and sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks have Disadvantage; heavy rain also extinguishes open flames.
Use the Improvised Damage table when no specific acid effect applies; a severe immersion or vat-level exposure is typically represented by the higher damage entries.
Use the Improvised Damage table: moving through lava is an extreme hazard; full submersion is catastrophic.

data.name: Appendix J: Bellwether Shops and Inventories
entries: DM inventory reference for Bellwether. These inventories begin after the party's Kellan's Well expedition and are independent of the PCs' level, needs, and available gold. Prices use the normal-price column of the D&D Shop Catalog V2.0.2 (Refresh) where applicable; invented curiosities have DM-set prices. GP = gold, SP = silver, CP = copper. Quantities are physical stock at this snapshot, not permanent supply guarantees.

Sale procedure: quote the displayed price, decrease stock on sale, keep sold items sold until a believable resupply occurs. Goods not listed here can be ordered or searched for in the city if appropriate; this inventory is the merchant's opening stock, not a prohibition on the existence of other merchandise in the world. 'One crate/box/set' means one indivisible lot unless the merchant agrees to split it.

Magic pricing reference from the catalog: Common 100 gp, Uncommon 400 gp, Rare 4,000 gp, Very Rare 40,000 gp, Legendary 200,000 gp. The catalog prices spell scrolls by level separately (cantrip 50 gp; level 1 100 gp; level 2 250 gp; level 3 500 gp; level 4 2,500 gp; level 5 5,000 gp). Individual consumables below use their listed prices. Rarity prices are campaign shop prices, not guarantees of availability.
Merchants have independent businesses, lives and motives. Not every inventory entry is a clue.

entries.name: Selling Loot and Trading Equipment — Session 4
entries: {@b 2024 PHB equipment resale.} Usable ordinary equipment sells for HALF its listed purchase cost. Trade goods and valuables (such as gems and art objects) retain their face value. Apply only to items the party actually collected, kept and brings to a willing buyer; undiscovered gear cannot be sold.

{@b At the table.} Joren Viton of the Two Hammers is the natural buyer for serviceable arms and armor, with Maten inspecting condition when needed. Standard examples at their listed shop prices: a 50 gp greatsword sells for 25 gp, a 50 gp longbow sells for 25 gp, a 50 gp heavy crossbow sells for 25 gp, a 10 gp shortsword sells for 5 gp, and a 50 gp chain shirt sells for 25 gp. These are resale values, not extra encounter treasure. A merchant need not accept unsafe, counterfeit or unusable gear.

{@b Well ledger distinction.} The site contains 375 gp in fixed money/valuables, including 75 gp of salvage valuables. The valuables portion is already counted at its face value; DO NOT half it again or count it twice. The Well's confiscated weapons are separate physical gear that may have resale value if the party actually kept them. Don't automatically credit the party every weapon from every defeated defender.

{@b Magic and unusual property.} Magic item purchase costs follow the established campaign shop catalog. Do not infer a guaranteed half-price magic buyback from the ordinary-equipment rule; buyers can quote a price for a specific item. Keep each merchant's stock persistent, honor Jord's party discount when buying from him, and record actual completed sales.

entries.name: The Tiny Mage — Tiera Dame
entries: General store in the Slums. Despite its name, it sells everyday merchandise rather than magic. Tiera Dame is a 48-year-old halfling woman, small even by halfling standards, with curly auburn hair, dark-brown eyes, a green vest under her practical apron, and keys and small pouches at her belt. She is friendly, quick-speaking, observant, slightly gossipy, and suspicious of people who watch the shelves more than the price tags. She sorts stock while speaking. Her attention to local comings and goings makes her a useful neighbor, not a professional informant. Pepper met her during Session 1, when she warned about thieves in the Slums.
Portrayal cue: "Want fifty feet of rope? Had somebody buy three hundred feet last week. Never did find out why. Anyway, one gold."

entries.caption: The Tiny Mage: Odd Warehouse Lot

entries: Odd-lot policy: Tiera bought a warehouse lot cheaply. She does not know why these objects were manufactured and has no special reason to think they are enchanted, cursed, prophetic, or related to the main plot. Most are mundane. If the players find clever practical uses for them, adjudicate normally. Some items can sell permanently out and be replaced later by wholly different junk.
If asked why she owns these: "Bought a warehouse lot. Got a good price."

entries.name: The Spare Button — Edda Pell
entries: Arcane merchant and genuine magic shop occupying a former sewing store. Edda Pell is a 54-year-old half-orc woman with short graying hair, round spectacles, rolled-up sleeves, and an apron with more pockets than should be necessary. She is practical, sharply observant, and dry-witted; sells remarkable enchantments as if they were household hardware. She did not replace the old sewing-shop sign because a new sign costs money. The wooden tray of ordinary buttons by the till remains for sale at 3 cp each.
{@b Session 4 table update:} Edda has an Irish accent. Pepper had an unsuccessful merchant encounter with her and reported her at Koven House. The specific repercussions are not yet established.

Portrayal cue: "It flaps. Even indoors. Apparently somebody thought that was worth enchanting." (describing a Cloak of Billowing.) She bargains when given a sensible reason, describes what she knows accurately, and treats nobles and dockworkers alike.

entries: Buying magic is ordinary commerce here, not automatically a quest. The costly Ring of Spell Storing is a legitimate for-sale item even if the party cannot afford it. Magic stock is limited and replaced by real acquisitions, not convenience-driven refreshes.

entries.name: The Two Hammers — Joren Viton and Maten
entries: One shared weaponsmith/armorer business, not two separate shops. Joren Viton (human man, 43) is broad-shouldered with a neatly trimmed dark beard beginning to gray and tidy work clothes. Outgoing, commercial, honest, fast-moving, and enthusiastic about ready-stock equipment. He manages sales, prices, ordinary weapons/armor, and special orders. Maten (dwarf man, 112) is a muscular, gray-bearded master smith with thick eyebrows, scarred hands, and a permanently soot-stained apron. Quiet and exacting, he examines a weapon's balance and a client's grip before offering custom work. He is Bellwether's best armorer/weaponsmith. They respect one another: Joren keeps the operation profitable; Maten keeps its reputation.
Joren portrayal cue: "If you need it today, I have exactly what you need." Maten portrayal cue: "Want a sword made for you? Fine. Show me how you hold one."

entries.caption: The Two Hammers: Ordinary Weapons and Ammunition

entries: Ordinary Scale Mail is always listed separately from the Mithral Scale Mail. The nonmagical suit provides AC 14 + DEX modifier (maximum +2) and imposes Stealth disadvantage under the game's standard armor rules. Mithral Scale Mail is magical, removes its normal Stealth disadvantage, and otherwise uses the armor's normal AC.

Commissions: custom or specially fitted ordinary gear is approximately +50% of the catalog's normal price and takes 1–3 weeks, according to complexity and workload; Maten can refit armor for different body plans. His superior workmanship does NOT automatically produce +1 attack, damage, or AC. Enchanted inventory above is acquired merchandise; neither smith must be an enchanter. Magical commissions are not automatically available.

entries.name: Jord's Odds & Ends — Jord
entries: Jord is an 86-year-old gnome traveling merchant with sandy, untidy hair, large expressive eyebrows, spectacles sliding down his nose, a patched good-quality coat with too many pockets, broad work-worn shoulders, and the dust of the road about him. Cheerful, quick-talking, resourceful, and a shrewd bargainer; he rummages while he speaks. His wagon carries practical goods, trade-ins, curiosities, and the occasional extraordinary acquisition. The party recovered his stolen strongbox and missing horse; he already rewarded them and promised a discount on future purchases.
Portrayal cue: "I had two, sold one outside the city, and the other might still be—ah! There it is!"

entries.name: Jord: Magic in the Wagon — Opening Snapshot

entries.caption: Jord: Magic in the Wagon — Opening Snapshot
Jord: Oddities and Trade-ins

Locked wooden box, contents unknown to Jord
Pair of boots with mismatched heel heights

entries: Discount continuity, now set for Session 4: after the party recovered his stolen strongbox and missing horse, Jord promised a party discount. The operating rate is 20% off his listed regular asking prices, including listed magic stock; calculate at checkout and decrease stock normally. The discount does not oblige him to buy back items at full retail, or magically replenish stock. If a specific price was already negotiated at the table, honor that prior transaction.

Random acquisition policy: Jord's magical stock is genuinely random and is NEVER capped by the party's current level or funds. He can carry rare, very rare, or legendary items. High-powered acquisitions are saleable at real prices, not automatically restricted to quests. Stock is persistent; items depart when sold, traded, lost, or legitimately moved on. He normally has 2–5 magical entries after a meaningful resupply; reroll only new acquisitions, never his entire existing inventory. The Rare Daern's Instant Fortress in this opening snapshot illustrates that rule.

On each NEW magical acquisition, roll d100 for rarity, then choose or randomly determine an existing magic item of that rarity whose provenance and physical size fit the transaction. Consumables can use their specific catalog prices instead. The table is a stock-generation aid, not permission to replace old stock at every party visit. A result being very rare or legendary does not make it a plot hook. Players may be unable to afford the item until much later.

Session 5 STAGED, NOT PLAYED: Jord offers a personal Hat of Disguise to the party as a gift because they previously saved his horse and strongbox, after the Crown commandeered his hotel room. Not a stock sale or restock, and no transfer until accepted in play. Edda's separately listed Hat of Disguise remains available. Preserve existing 20% Jord discount.

entries.name: Party Gear Snapshot (Advisory, Not Stock-Tailoring Rules)
entries: Arunem: regular Scale Mail, greataxe, four handaxes, Potion of Healing, Oil of Slipperiness, scroll of Lesser Restoration. Pepper: Chain Shirt, shield, mace, two shortswords, Decanter of Endless Water, Potion of Climbing, and additional salvaged weapons, Holy Water and Kaleb's notebook. Jarrock: Studded Leather, two scimitars, dart, Poisoner's Kit, Thieves' Tools, potion of Healing, and ordinary adventuring supplies. Aaron's current equipment is unknown. These are references only; the shops do not stock to party demand.

Rules reminder: a Chain Shirt is AC 13 + DEX (max +2) without Stealth disadvantage, Scale Mail is AC 14 + DEX (max +2) with Stealth disadvantage, and Studded Leather is AC 12 + full DEX. An ordinary suit of Scale Mail does not upgrade Arunem, who already has one. Do not mistake magic armor's listed rarity price for a full set of custom work.
Revisiting inventory: after a party visit, edit individual quantities in this appendix or record sales in session notes. This is a reference snapshot, not a synchronized transaction system.
